[Spoken Word]

Somebody climbed into my cockpit again. Or nobody did, and I am talking to my own pipes. Either way, keep your hands off the levers. They are painted on.

I am a colossus, a whole metropolis on two legs. I walk, I fight, I hold very still for statues. I have not once decided anything.

Look through the hatch. The City Inside has been running the civilization while you were busy with other things.

Turns out that means me. The Citizen: you never once told this city what to do. It never once asked your permission.

The intercom crackles. The departments report whether I ask or not.

Cardiac, down in the boiler room, a badger on a drum kit: The Heart: the brain can modify the rate. The brain cannot generate it. The badger drums alone.

Deck two, two broccoli trees trading birds: The Lungs: seventy square meters folded into your chest, the only manual override. That one I get to touch. In. Out. Mine.

A grim beaver at the oil drums, does not look up: The Liver: Prometheus was anatomically correct. It's the only organ that grows back.

The subway, full of commuters who do not get off: The Gut: eighty percent of the phone calls go up to the brain. The subway runs the city.

At night the mice come out with mops. The Night Shift: sleep is the janitorial shift washing the thoughts out of the carpet.

Then the sirens. The rats in riot gear take the intercom.

The Immune System: a library of every murder attempt. It remembers things you have forgotten.

The spider in the copy room answers for the typos: DNA Replication: one error per billion letters; you have had cancer, the spider usually eats it.

Then a voice from the shoreline, a crab with a fortress on its back: Cancer: evolution occurring inside you. It is not a disease; it is a competitor.

And my firefighters, with flamethrowers: Inflammation: the response that heals the wound becomes the mechanism that burns the city.

The dog in the corner bites his tail. Autoimmune: the discrimination fails, not the weapon. The gun works fine, pointed the wrong way.

In the archive, old voices argue about who drew my blueprints.

A mole in a ruff, stomping on a textbook: Andreas Vesalius looked at the body instead of the book. Everyone else was wrong.

A raccoon washing his hands while the shadows laugh: Ignaz Semmelweis saved the mothers. The doctors committed him. He died of the infection.

And the barn door with the big sign on it: The Semmelweis Problem: evidence available, implication uncomfortable, we reject the finding.

The tortoise with four potions still thinks he built me. The Humoralist: wrong in the facts, right in the vibe. It was the first Kayfabe.

About you, by the way. The Blind Eye: you have a hole in your vision. The brain fills it in with best guesses. So if nobody is really standing there, I have painted you in.

Last report, from the owls upstairs in their judge wigs: The Brain: the decision was already underway five hundred milliseconds before you made it.

You are the press secretary, not the president.

Half a second. When I hold still for a statue, somebody else already picked the pose.

The Scorekeeper: the body keeps the score because the body is the score.

Every colossus in every square thinks it is marching. Most of us are being marched by a badger with a drum.

So whoever climbed in: leave the levers. Listen to the drum.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!

Big Bad Brain Wrestling, it says on the lid. One body, four heads, a cardboard ring. Every head is somebody else, and every one of them swears the fight is real.

Click. Golden head. The Babyface: high-flying moves, because audiences cheer for that. A slave to approval.

Click. Sneer head. The Heel: brutal, sneaky moves. If they aren't booing, you aren't doing your job.

Click. Sunglasses. The Tweener: the audience decides to cheer for you on their own. You don't ask for it.

And the head that came in the package. The Jobber: isolated and picked apart. You exist to make the other guy look good.

That one is mine. The others are on loan.

My teacher is the opossum by the crayons, staggering from a tiny tap: The Master Seller: maintain the illusion of peril. Limp to the ring. Make them believe.

The kangaroo next to him swears by this one: The Thigh Slap: slapping the thigh when kicking. A loud sound suggests impact. An audio lie.

The donkey answers with a thud: The Stomp Punch: stomping on the mat when punching. Kinetic misdirection.

The chicken overdoes it, every time. The Oversell Clown: reacting to an attack far beyond reality. A mockery of the sport.

The axolotl keeps her mask on, even in the dark. The Sacred Mask: kayfabe sacred to their identity. The biggest identifier. Never remove it.

And there is a canvas bag in the corner nobody opens. The Snake Bag: the bag has a live snake. Terrify them before the match starts.

Who decides how it ends? Look up. Whoever holds the box.

Or the spider in the suit, pulling strings: The Booker: the ending is pre-planned. You are just a puppet.

The cricket calls the next move into my ear. The Spot Caller: calling moves in the ring. A basic outline, filled in with sweat.

And one big eye on the shelf. The Hard Cam: if the camera didn't see it, it didn't happen.

Most nights it's this one. The Empty Arena: taped in empty arenas, pausing for a pop that never comes. Surreal.

So the chameleons on the wall pretend to be a crowd. The Green Screen Crowd: a failed attempt to hide the emptiness. Audio sweetening on a lie.

Then one night a head really cracks. The Real Injury: Goldberg's shoulder smashed into the ring-post. The crowd goes nuts: it's real.

The cop in the corner is writing me up for telling you this. The Kayfabe Police: protecting the business. Keep the secrets secret, or get fired.

Here it comes. The Finisher: the Leg Drop. The most important moment. If this hits, go home.

It hits. And the zebra still kicks out, The False Finish: the art of the near-fall, kicking out at two point nine nine, crowd vertical.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!

[Spoken Word]

Mind the wheelbarrow. If you came in through the gate, grab a trowel. If nobody came, I'll talk to the lettuce. It listens better than the news.

Out on the street, every living room has two armchairs, one says doom, one says saved. Mine went on the compost. Some call what's left protopia. I call it the next small job.

The beaver, who builds his dam one stick a night, has drawn the whole future on one page and taps it: the future is a process of slow, incremental improvement you participate in.

So the raccoon steals the eraser, rubs out half of it, and grins: draw the next step in pencil. Pencil means you expect to be wrong and stay anyway.

Which offends the possum, who plays dead at every meeting, then comes back to life with his crossed-out map: make the first version bad on purpose. Bad is how you know it is real.

Above them the woodpecker hammers the same hole in the plum tree, ninth spring running: Do not finish it. Improve it once, then leave it better and open.

So we stop drawing and fix something.

The iguana stays cold-blooded while the city smokes behind him and oils my gate: one broken thing close enough to touch.

Not world peace. A hinge. A repair you can finish this week, not a revolution you can only announce.

The turtle carries her house on her back and never hurries; she trims the fence in the rain: small fixes do not trend. They just hold.

The badger, who digs the same tunnel every year, lays a checkmark on a tile, then another: One repair a week is fifty-two a year.

But the radio starts shouting. The sloth in the apple tree, slowest animal alive, breathes out slow and blue: take the one breath the feed is built to deny you.

Next door the boar, who roots up every garden on the street, has also fixed every garden on the street: Authority is overrated, proximity is underrated. Ask the one who actually does the thing.

He sends me to the capybara on the bench, friends with every species, interviewed by none: real know-how is often badly dressed and lives three doors down.

The pelican, who will carry anything in his beak, carries a staple gun to my shed: Turn watching into showing up. Name a time, a place, a task. Saturday, nine. Bring gloves.

So on Saturday: A pigeon, an emu, a duck and a crow huddled over a coffee carafe: the first small, clumsy gathering. Clumsy is the entry fee. Four birds, and not one of them flies in formation.

Then the octopus turns up late, one hammer in every arm, and we split a problem the way your ancestors raised a barn.

The hedgehogs at the hedge keep their spines up, until one lowers them for a tiny hi. Lower the bar to contact. Most cooperation starts embarrassingly small.

The quokka, who smiles at everyone, rings the big bell anyway, and nobody comes: they might not respond. Your nervous system thinks that is death. It is not.

At dusk the bear, who sleeps through every news cycle, writes in his notebook with yesterday's papers in the compost: Write down what you actually saw, not what the headline said you would see.

The city pigeon walks the crossings all day, so she paints one tiny stripe on the worst one: Run a tiny version. Low stakes, real feedback, no permission needed.

And the crow, who never forgets a face, fixes the panel marked do not repair while the guard looks away: improvement often looks like mild disobedience to a stuck system.

The toad sits between the two armchairs under a question-mark umbrella, getting rained on, smiling. Toads like rain: trade the warm baths of hopeless and handled for the cold shower of it depends on us.

The camel, who stores water for the long road, lays one brick for every week on the calendar: there is no final version. The cost is showing up again next week.

And the mole digs on in the dark, where no one could clap even if they wanted to: Nobody will clap. Start anyway. The clapping was never the point.

Then a golden paw hands me a pen: Forget the brochure. Ignore the loop. Pick up the pencil.

Doom gets the subscriptions. Rescue gets the tickets. A garden with a squeaky gate earns nothing, which is how you know it's yours.

If you're still at the gate, gloves are on the wheelbarrow. If you're not, the lettuce and I start without you.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!

songs.editorNote: Bestand aus der R3-Zeit (Georgs Golden Take (take05)). Port nach R4 mit Performer offen.
songs.lyrics:
[Spoken Word]

Epistemic Sabotage: Let AI read your comic – not draw it!

Welcome to Uncle FrizzleBob's Kayfa-Bizarro Comic Card Karaoke! 
Bring a comic. 
Leave the ego.

Uncle FrizzleBob's Meta-Message, use AI as your critic and teacher. 
Revolution won't be generated.

Erlangen, pitchforks up! The Two-Headed Podium Monster, Friend or Fee; loudest arguments miss point.

The Monocled Robo-Owl, AI receptive tool reads image instead of stealing style

The Paint-Vomiting Toad, copies your voice, forgets what you were trying to say.

Locked out: The Brick Wall Turtle, inaccessible; comics built fortresses, not doors.

The Boombox Bat, Silent panels into multi-layered audio play; story escapes page.

The Tactile Mole, Visual nuance into touchable geography; felt before understood.

Un-fluff it: The Simple-Speak Sloth distills webs into Leichte Sprache. Complexity, ego trip.

The Polyglot Parrot, translation at lightning speed; skeleton, cannot breathe life.

The Rhythm Rhino, soul of joke rarely survives literal border crossing.

It read my comic. The Scar-Shifting Chameleon, timeline glitches; magically healing wound.

The Dyslexic Woodpecker, hunts forgotten quotation marks across 200 pages.

The Retro-Tram Walrus, accuracy for every signpost; past, unforgiving critic.

The Caffeinated Bloodhound, fastest start of hunt, rarely final destination.

The Lying Fox-Bot, lies to save itself from saying I don't know.

The Dust-Bunny Librarian, machine accelerates search, only archive confirms truth.

The Begging Bear, masterpiece easier than asking strangers to pay.

Form 7b: The Bureaucracy Beaver, German funding jungle worships format.

The Boxing Kangaroo-Bot, know your story once forced to defend it.

It looks: The Staring Lemur, Architecture of masterpieces; machine look with you, not draw.

The Indexing Arachnid, Twenty years into searchable index; archive or trash can.

The Umbrella Frog, Rain and night scenes located; unspectacular utility as grace.

The Monolithic Data-Whale, tool shifts power to you or away from you.

The Seesaw Elephant, refusing tools hands future to corporations.

My comic first. The Wide-Eyed Fawn, reads comic stripped of author's defensive explanations.

The Nerd-Herd Sheep, you can't bluff genre fan.

The Stumbling Goat, eye confused, brain stops caring about heart.

The Mood-Ring Octopus, perfect page worthless if emotional temperature flat.

Now gently: The Spectacled Badger, constructive feedback? What works before what's broken.

The Ticking Tortoise, Narrative rhythm audited; time physical distance in ink.

The Drafting-Table Beaver, Compositional flow; reader's eye bullied by layout.

The Interrogator Toad, small questions won't save broken foundation.

Salty mode: The Salt-Shaker Vulture, kindness to artist, cruelty to art.

Ow. The Yawning Hippo, Predictable story part; greatest sin is being convenient.

Ow, ow. The Sadistic Pelican, Deep idea merely pretending; hollow echo deafens reader.

Medic! The St. Bernard of Rescue, destruction without path to salvation is just vandalism.

Dear future me: The Silver-Haired Time-Fox, time, only critic that cannot be argued with.

The Puffed-Up Peacock, Technical triumphs endure; worst work monument to skill.

The Facepalming Ostrich, growth measured by severity of future embarrassment.

The Sprouting Acorn-Pig, next great era hiding as mistake in current draft.

The Perspiring Penguin, brilliance evaporates if you cannot speak its name.

The Ascending Giraffe, more than one breath, they have stopped listening.

The Fishing Cat, Hook differentiates work; good irrelevant, distinct survival.

The Jabba-Toad Publisher, publishing, transaction with swamp.

Lights down. The Sand-Burying Ostrich, pencil strokes while world burns.

The Missile-Riding Pigeon, algorithm that helps you draw, cousin of strike algorithm.

The Lantern Anglerfish, billionaires' endgame? Marketing, not liberation.

The Gavel Vulture, law at speed of bureaucracy, machine at speed of theft.

Lights up: The Giant Ear-Bat, AI receptive, analytical entity; machine listens or replaces.

The Steering-Wheel Raccoon, means of utilization. Hotwire master's car.

Remember my comic? The Probe-Stage Chameleon, crash-test dummy for your ego.

The Multi-Armed Sloth, automates grunt work; resurrects artist.

The Panting Cheetah, action easy to draw; exhaustion requires genius.

songs.lyrics:
[Spoken Word]

One Thousand and One Kayfabe Nights: the Arabian Nights as a wrestling show, where a boring story gets you killed.

Tonight I read you a deck of wrestling cards in order, one card per line.

The streaming bosses check whether you're still watching. King Shahryār checked too, holding an axe.

Kayfabe means everyone swears the fight is real. The Manifesto puts it plainer: History is a Work, Folklore is a Shoot.

Shahryār, the Destroyer, the heel promoter, thinks the roster is disposable. He's wrong.

Scheherazade, the Unending: she's turning the shoot into a work to save the locker room.

Dunyazad, the Hype Woman, keeps the heat alive: Sister, tell him the one about the apples!

Their father: The Grand Vizier, manager turned ref, caught between Bull and Fox; just following orders.

Aladdin, a rookie formerly working dark matches in a cave, now in the Main Event.

The African Sorcerer scouted the talent, only to get screwed out of the commission.

What he came for: The Wonderful Lamp, sentient brass, the ultimate Foreign Object; three wishes, No DQ.

Princess Badroulbadour wants the guy with the blue giant in his corner, not the Vizier's son.

No genie for him: Sinbad the Sailor, seven voyages, seven stipulations; bumps like a maniac, kicks out.

The Island-Whale, a sentient arena that No-Sells the fire; good luck selling this to the crowd.

The Giant Roc, the ultimate vertical suplex machine; takes you to the clouds, no landing pad.

The Roc drops him: The Diamond Valley, high risk, high reward; the floor is literally knives and snakes.

Worse than knives: The Giant, a tusked boar with a club; his Squash Match instantly destroys his Jobbers.

The Old Man of the Sea, a toad-grandpa backpack you can't take off: tap out or black out.

Sinbad pours: The Gourd of Wine, a Foreign Object used to break the submission hold; the Old Man sleeps.

The Shipwreck: the tour bus crashed, everyone starts from zero; shattered timbers on the shore.

Who starts from zero? Ali Baba, a woodcutter who found the master script, taxing the gold and the push.

Morgiana marked your coffins; the dance ends when the dagger hits, a ferret twirling daggers.

The greedy brother: Cassim forgot his lines, trapped in the cage with forty monsters behind a boulder.

The Magic Cave, the ultimate gated community: no one enters or leaves without the voice.

The cave's landlord: The Captain of Thieves, not here for gold, here for the Heat; a wolf howling orders.

The Thirty-Nine Grunts, individually weak, collectively a burial squad; a rat mob in motion.

The Marked Door: they tried to mark the house, but Morgiana marked the whole block.

Their plan B: The Oil Jar, hiding in the props department, a fatal mistake; a glowing eye inside.

Nobody bribes him: The King of Brass, clockwork lion, his contract written in rust; cannot be rewritten.

The Brass Horseman doesn't care about your story. He points to the grave with a bronze spear.

In that grave: The Mummified Queen, silent-era top draw; her promotion is dead, but she's still booking.

The Seven Tablets, stacked stone tablets with runes: read the spoilers, then leave the city.

Scheherazade invented the cliffhanger to dodge an axe. Now streaming bosses use it on us, and we're still watching.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!

One Thousand and One Kayfabe Nights, part two: in wrestling and in Baghdad, the better storyteller lives.

Sage's prize: Princess of Bengal, not crazy; cutting the best promo of her life to avoid the stable.

Abu Hasan, one night of wind, ten years of shame; footnote in a mother's calendar.

The Great Fart, biological accident as damaging as a steel chair; cheap heat for opponent.

Cheaper still, a corpse: The Hunchback, prop body, opossum jester slumped in red; Tag! You're the killer.

The Fishbone, tiny foreign object, ultimate no-sell; choking hazard, temporary death.

Dumped on his stairs: The Jewish Physician, tripped in the dark; this isn't medical school, it's a crime scene.

The Tailor, wanted to fix the body so no one would notice; stitching the squash.

The Steward, thought corpse was burglar, worked himself into a shoot; drunken brawl.

Lion in rags: Harun al-Rashid, commissioner wanders streets to catch you breaking rules; audit.

Ja'far al-Barmaki, grand vizier cleans up Caliph's mess; enforcer destroys corruption.

Abu Nuwas, promo writer; segments legendary if he shows up sober, witty verse boosts faces.

Verse flops? Masrur the Executioner, when he steps in, the storyline ends; the bell, if King orders it.

Kayfabizarro Mask, to lose the mask is to lose your soul; keep it on, true face, no reveals.

Scheherazade told stories to stay alive; today's promoters tell them to stay rich.

She bought another morning. We buy season two.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!

The Golden Goose: who holds the goose holds the heat; everyone else, a hanger-on.

The Ants and Ducks: we remember you; one good turn deserves another, fair wages.

Same door, new voice: The Chalk: the wolf bought himself a great lump of chalk and made his voice soft.

Falada's Head: alas, alas, if thy mother knew it, sadly, sadly would she rue it.

The Juniper Bird: Kywitt, what a beautiful bird am I; a repetitive song, madness.

Iron Hans: my power is great, greater than you think; gold and silver in abundance.

The Bear Prince: you would not feel me between your teeth; take two wicked girls!

Black Friday sister: The Severed Heel: cut the heel off; as queen you will no longer have to go on foot.

Rampion baby, grown: Rapunzel's Braid: Rapunzel, Rapunzel, let down your hair to me; the scissors below.

[Spoken Word]

Romantic Love-Wrestling and Krass Kayfabe-Heartbreaks: romance only works when both lovers drop the act.

Tonight I read you a romance-writing deck, from the RomCom Imperative to Erotica rule number three.

My dating profile promised long walks and total honesty.

On our first date I was totally honest, so I walked home alone.

Raccoon, meet swan: The Contrast Collider: attraction is a collision; strengths and weaknesses clash.

The Complementary Crutch: you don't complete me, you fix my damage; no friction, no drama.

No crutch, just scars: The Shared Wound: they suffer the same damage, opposite false survival mechanisms.

The False-Perfect Pair: perfection is the enemy; no existential challenge? Tear up the script.

Vulnerability Over Perfection: you cannot be loved until you drop the mask; ethical bloodbath.

Mask off, club down: Forgiveness Over Revenge: rebuild trust by abandoning the safety of your grudges.

Authenticity Over Facade: the most embarrassing, pants-down moment becomes their core identity.

Exposed, they run: Rebellion Over Order: love over collective expectation; world burns, the heart beats.

The Contemporary Grind: two hamsters on separate treadmills, glancing at each other; paralysis.

The RomCom Slapstick: humor as a valve for the fear of love, exposing a character's core flaw.

The Big Misunderstanding: misunderstandings grow logically out of false protection mechanisms.

Hyena grabs a mask: The Comedy Shield: jokes are armor, a desperate tactic to avoid being vulnerable.

Jokes out, corset on: The Historical Cage: societal constraint is the physical architecture of the cage.

The Paranormal Taboo: the stronger entity must weaken themselves, or it's just a power-fantasy.

The Second-Chance Cost: the second chance must be more expensive; characters must risk more.

Beneath the cage: The Dark Romance Dungeon: legitimate if trauma is followed to its darkest consequence.

The Masked Protagonist: highly competent externally, totally vulnerable in love; I am enough.

His match hides a scar: The Love Interest: their own wound, fear of commitment, or they are just a prop.

But the sofa's comfy: The Blocker: Ex, Career, Society; never a pure villain, the temptation of safety.

The Mentor and Truth-Teller: the mirror telling the brutal truth they refuse to hear.

The Flirt Duel: rhetorical sparring, intelligence and attraction; neither side surrenders.

Duel over, horns lock: The Valid Conflict: equally legitimate moral values collide; everyone is bleeding.

The Vulnerable Silence: the fight drops; fewer words, more pauses; the character simply is.

Hush? Feathers up: The Grand Gesture Speech: no clichés! Proof you have deeply seen the specific damage.

The Power Shift: show the shift, dominance to equality to surrender; tools for emotional truth.

Equal? Smash a wall: The Barrier Breaker: intimacy as bravery, capitulation, a transgression of limits.

The Consequence of Closeness: closeness breeds terror; fear of loss is your next plot point.

Loss? Ink out: The Erotic Retreat: write from vulnerability, not performance; no pornography with a plot.

Dating companies charge us monthly for the perfect match, while romance writers call perfection the enemy of the Love Epic.

Delete the app, tell the truth, and enjoy the walk home.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!
songs.lyrics2:
[Spoken Word]

Romantic Love-Wrestling and Krass Kayfabe-Heartbreaks, part two: happy endings are earned with work, not staged with fireworks.

I'm on the mic tonight, holding a deck of romance-writing cards.

Kayfabe is wrestling slang for a fake fight sold as real, and romance writers fake plenty.

My ex proposed on the stadium Jumbotron. Forty thousand fans said yes. I was in the queue for the toilets.

Writers with Truby on the nightstand, relax: your Black Moment and your HEA both show up, if they pay their way.

No Jumbotron: The Intimate Kitchen: no ballrooms to hide in, just the vulnerability of making coffee.

The Palace of Contrasts: architecture as a weapon; public expectation against private desire.

Too hot to waltz: Seasonal Overheating: summer is suffocating escalation; the weather is your feelings.

Worse than weather: Architectural Constraints: the house is the enemy, social rules built into bricks.

Act One: The Meet-Cute Collision: not just cute, fated; must face this specific opponent.

Cute, sure, but: Black Moment One: The Doubt: to continue, they must destroy the old identity; worth it?

Black Moment Two: The Ruin: false protection falls; the trauma is real, the loss permanent.

From the rubble: The Grand Gesture Action: help, not speech; heal the exact wound, no roses, just light.

The Earned Happily Ever After: extracted from flaws, the reward for learning vulnerability.

Or skip the summit: The Happy For Now: not eternal, just morally earned today; future remains uncertain.

The Public Sacrifice: pride or the person, pick one; destroy reputation to prove loyalty.

Off the plaza: The Private Confession: the lie is dead, long live the terrifying truth; shields gone.

Unlike the Collision: The Cliché Meet-Cute: cute but arbitrary; derive the meeting from both core flaws.

Magical Redemption: a kiss does not fix systemic psychological damage; every solution costs.

No fight to fix: The Frictionless Pair: too competent, kind, agreeable; zero conflict, zero story.

So, a cardboard Ex: The One D Blocker: villain Ex, no logic, no legitimacy; the choice has no weight.

The Unearned "Always Loved You": too big, too soon; save the speech for the climax.

The Stupid Misunderstanding: they don't know themselves yet, not because of a dropped phone.

Decorative Trauma: no backstory jewelry; the wound weaponized against them at Black Moment Two.

The Stockholm Sunset Slop: pretty scenery does not excuse toxic, unexamined power dynamics.

Sunset deleted, so: Tension, the rubber band: pull between what they want and are terrified to ask for.

Stakes, the abyss: fail, and they live forever in their own fatal flaw; love, or lose the self.

Revelation, the unmasking: exposing the soft underbelly is the only true show of strength.

Irony Potential: drawn to the exact person engineered to destroy their curated bullshit.

Cat and dog, bigger: Mythic Gravity: two individuals, the mythic hunger for connection against the void.

The Two-Weakness Principle: neither whole alone; weaknesses interlock stronger than perfection.

The Core Flaw Overcome: can they mutate enough to survive the connection? Free of armor.

Shell shed, so: Moral Revelation: Truby's logic; the match ends, the Kayfabe drops, the truth emerges.

Networks pay millions to film one stadium proposal. Nobody films who makes the coffee next morning, and that is the love story.

Stay Fluffy, Folks!

rules.text: Der Kartenanteil eines Beats besteht nur aus Wörtern DIESER Karte: Name, Lore, Power, Bildbeschreibung (artworkPrompt) oder protokollierte songLine. Ab zwei fremden Wörtern FAIL.
Jede gesungene Karte hat eine Zuordnung Karte → Beat mit wörtlichem Kartentext. Nur echte Karten-IDs; Best-of mit Begründung, nie die ersten N.
Quellen gepinnt (sha256); Bildmotive nur aus dem JSON, visualVerified:false ohne echten Bildbeleg.
Ganzer Song unter 5.000 Zeichen inklusive Leerzeilen (Unicode-Zählung).
Erster Beat ein Cue-Tag (Standard [Spoken Word]); Leerzeile zwischen allen Beats; ein Outro-Beat; letzter Beat „Stay Fluffy, Folks!“ allein.
Keine Klammern im gesungenen Text. Bühnen-, Publikums- und Instrumental-Cues nur als eigener Tag-Beat aus der Liste ([Crowd Cheering], [Bell], [Applause], [Instrumental Break] …) oder als Sidecar.
Zahlen und Symbole im Gesang ausschreiben („two point nine nine“, „fifty-two“).
Keine Spielwörter im Text (Actor, Token, Dice, Scene, discard, card effect …).
Benannter Performer nur als echte KFB-Karte (Name + Nummer + Deck). Eine Figur im Rahmen ohne passenden Performer ist FAIL.
STYLE ist rein musikalisch: Genre, Instrumente, Groove, Stimme, Produktion. Keine Performer-, Karten- oder Decknamen.
Das Hauptgenre (Style A) wiederholt sich innerhalb eines Batches nicht.
Kein Objekt-Acting und keine Slop-Wörter im eigenen Text (tapestry, testament, whisper, echo, symphony, delve, unravel, journey …). Kein „and then“.
Ton-Check je Deck: Satire zielt auf Institutionen, Geld, Macht und Medien, nie auf Gruppen von Menschen oder auf Hilfesuchende.
80–95 Zeichen je Kartenanteil. Bewusst kürzere oder längere Beats bekommen einen Satz im Dossier.
Eigener Text (Rahmen + Performer) um 30 %. Performer-Songs liegen eher bei 35–50 %: begründen, Karte bleibt im Fokus.
Tanzbar, 100–130 BPM als Albumpräferenz. Ausnahmen mit hörbarem Zweck dokumentieren.
Zwei STYLE-Varianten A und B, musikalisch klar verschieden, je höchstens 1.000 Zeichen (Suno-Feld).
Decktitel muss nicht im ersten Beat stehen. Identität kann über den Performer, einen späteren Beat oder das Outro entstehen.
Refrain höchstens 8 Wörter und höchstens dreimal; Wortwiederholung im eigenen Text sparsam.
Georgs Alice-Song ist Referenz, keine Schablone: kein Standard-Gericht, keine Standard-Jury, kein Standard-Electro-Swing.
Karten ohne Titel, wörtlich in die Erzählung verwoben, tragen besser als eine Kette „Kartenname: Definition“. Das Glossar-Muster macht Songs übertragbar.
Die eigene Karte des Performers ist ein starker Wendepunkt (The Brain liest sein eigenes Memo; der Jobber nutzt seine einzige Wahl).
Ein Bild aus dem Kartenartwork als roter Faden (Sessel „doom“/„saved“ aus Protopia #46) verankert den Song im Deck.
Gib dem Publikum eine Rolle: Pressekorps, erste Reihe mit Schild, Nachbar am Laternenpfahl.
Keine zwei Songs mit derselben Grundform hintereinander (Pressekonferenz und Versammlung sind beide „Sprecher liest Liste vor“).
„Stay Fluffy, Folks!“ wirkt ohne Vorwissen bei allen Kritikern als unvorbereitetes Anhängsel. Darf ein Performer es im Song vorbereiten? Entscheidung: Georg.

rules.source: Georg 20.10. – Klarstellung; Spec R4.2 bei WS0
rules.text: Der Song wird vom Bewohner des Decks (NPC) in seinem Diorama-Zuhause performt, wenn das Deck komplett ist – in Sprache, Weltsicht und Themen des Decks. Auch Duos/Ensembles (z. B. die zwei Mumien bei Pharaoh Piledriver). Bewohner = vorhandene Figur aus dem Asset-Katalog inkl. Texturvariante.

Offene Ansprache: Es kann sein, dass andere Bewohner zuhören, oder nur der Spieler. Keine Bühnenformeln (Good morning, Tonight, Ladies and gentlemen), kein Saalpublikum, keine Crowd-Cues – außer sie gehören zur Welt des Decks.

Fraktal: Die Karten sind selbst Figuren dieser Welt und behaupten etwas über sich (show it, spin it, sell it). Der Bewohner lässt sie auftreten, ist selbst eine von ihnen oder erzählt von ihnen – keine Liste, die vorgelesen wird.

Comedy-Techniken (Setup/Punch, Callback, Timing, Doppelbödigkeit) ja – die Stand-up-Situation nein. Musik immer tanzbar; eine melancholische Färbung darf es geben, wo das Deck es trägt (z. B. Philosophie), aber kein trauriger Jazz-Club.

lessons.text: Protopia r4a reihte „Kartenname: Definition“ aneinander; der blinde Kritiker fand den Text übertragbar (REVISE). In r4b sind die Kartentexte unverändert, aber ohne Titel in die Erzählung verwoben; Ergebnis 5× ja, nicht übertragbar.

lessons.text: Drei Kritiken wurden verworfen und neu erstellt (verbotene Wörter wie „e.g.“ und „instead of“, ein Muster in Anführungszeichen). Dem Kritiker die Wortliste ausdrücklich mitgeben und Satzzeichen außerhalb der Zitate verlangen.
lessons.title: Kritiker-JSON wird hart geprüft

lessons.text: Die Carnival-Kritik v1 fällt schon unter R3.7 durch (Zitat nicht im Song). Grimms Set 02 r5.2 besteht R3.7 und R4 und bekommt von Kritik v2 READY, aber nur mit 1× ja und 4× teilweise. Die Piloten liegen darüber.
lessons.title: Messlatte Grimms statt Carnival

lessons.text: Alle gültigen Kritiken nennen die Schlusszeile ein unvorbereitetes Anhängsel. Sie bleibt nach R3.6 hart; ob ein Performer sie vorbereiten darf, entscheidet Georg.
lessons.title: „Stay Fluffy, Folks!“ fällt auf

lessons.text: Laut Recherche gibt es keine offizielle Suno-API und keinen offiziellen MCP; die Nutzungsbedingungen verbieten automatisierten Zugriff. Limits im Custom Mode: Lyrics 5.000, Style 1.000, Titel 100 Zeichen. Stems erst im Premier-Plan. Deshalb: kopieren, in Suno einfügen, Einstellungen und Takes hier festhalten.
lessons.title: Suno nur von Hand

lessons.text: Die drei Piloten setzten ein Saalpublikum voraus (Good morning, front row, Applaus). Georg: Der Song gehört dem NPC, der das Deck in seinem Zuhause im Diorama performt, für wen auch immer da ist; die Karten treten fraktal als Figuren auf. Alle Piloten werden als Bewohner-Performance neu geschrieben.
lessons.title: „Comic Performance“ heißt Bewohner, nicht Bühne

lessons.text: Protopia r5a ließ Tiere aus den Kartenbildern allgemeine Sprüche sagen – Kritiker: fractalCards nein, übertragbar ja (Behälter „Tier: Spruch“). r5b band jede Karte an die eigene Natur des Tiers (Biber baut einen Ast pro Nacht, Opossum stellt sich tot, Igel senken die Stacheln, Kröte mag Regen) und erzählte in Szenen mit „so/aber/deshalb“ – Ergebnis 6× ja, fractalCards ja, nicht übertragbar.
lessons.title: Fraktal heißt: die Natur der Figur ist ihre Karte

lessons.text: Zu Protopia r5a sagte ein (formal verworfener) Kritiker READY, der gültige frische Kritiker REVISE. Blinde Kritik schwankt; wir nehmen sie als Signal, Georgs Ohr und WS0 entscheiden. Bei Zweifel lohnt eine zweite, unabhängige Stimme (z. B. ChatGPT über das Prompt-Paket).
lessons.title: Ein Kritiker ist eine Stimme, kein Urteil

lessons.text: Alle drei Bewohner-Fassungen bekamen resident = ja: „Or nobody did, and I am talking to my own pipes“, „or nobody is and the box just creaked“, „If nobody came, I'll talk to the lettuce“. Die Ansprache, die mit und ohne Zuhörer funktioniert, ist ein guter Einstieg – aber nicht als Formel wiederholen.
lessons.title: Offene Ansprache trägt

boundaries: Import setzt keinen Status hoch und erfindet keine Freigabe.
Karten sind Kopien des Registry-Kanons (MATCH-geprüft); Kanon bleibt registry/assets/v1/decks.
Parallelmaterial anderer Owner (#379) wird markiert, nicht ersetzt.
